"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:5312, a Portuguese-text feature.

What it does: this component is silent in English, Spanish, German, French, Italian and
code, and it switches on inside Portuguese prose (Brazilian in the harvest: "Brasil",
"Produto", ".com.br" sites). Its activation is largest on Portuguese articles and
prepositions (" a", " do", " os", " na", " ao") and on the first piece of content words
(" plataforma", " nova", "Produto"), weaker on connectives and endings ("que", "e", "de",
"ção"), and slightly negative on " para".

How the program predicts it: it keeps, per document, the share of tokens so far that
look Portuguese (a list of common Portuguese words, or a token with Portuguese-only
letters or endings such as ã, õ, ç, nh, lh, -ção, -mente). The share is a running
average with a prior, so it starts low and grows as Portuguese text accumulates, and it
resets at each document boundary. Each token's prediction is that share times a weight
for the token: articles and prepositions 1.0, other word starts 0.7, other words 0.5,
punctuation and digits 0.2, and the weak words "de", "que", "e", "se" 0.4, "para" -0.3.
The first token of a row gets a constant 0.15, the average activation there.
"""

import re

READS = ()

PT_WORDS = frozenset(
    """de do da dos das que não uma uns umas um para pra com é são mais como mas também
    muito muita você vocês pelo pela pelos pelas isso isto esta este esse essa esses essas
    ser foi ele ela eles elas nos nas seu sua seus suas ao aos às pode podem ter tem está
    estão já sobre entre quando até porque ainda então depois antes onde qual quais sem
    mesmo ou se há era seja foram nosso nossa meu minha dele dela desde cada todo toda
    todos todas outro outra grande bem aqui hoje ano anos dia dias vez vezes pessoas
    pessoa fazer faz fazem sendo muitos muitas menos pois embora através durante contra
    após sob logo agora assim só nem tudo nada algum alguma alguns algumas nenhum nenhuma
    outros outras ver deve devem produto produtos serviço serviços empresa cliente clientes
    preço site página forma tipo cidade país brasil brasileiro brasileira usuário usuários
    dados dado uso melhor melhores novo nova novos novas sistema segundo lugar parte casa
    tempo vida mundo ponto caso fim quer querer""".split()
)
ARTICLES = frozenset("a o as os do da dos das no na nos nas ao aos um uma é mas".split())
WEAK = frozenset("de que e se".split())
PT_LETTERS = re.compile("[ãõçáéíóúâêôàÃÕÇÁÉÍÓÚÂÊÔÀ]")
PT_ENDINGS = ("ção", "ções", "mente", "ando", "endo", "indo")


def looks_portuguese(text, word):
    return (
        word in PT_WORDS
        or bool(PT_LETTERS.search(text))
        or "nh" in word
        or "lh" in word
        or word.endswith(PT_ENDINGS)
    )


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        pt_sum, count = 0.0, 0
    else:
        _, pt_sum, count = carry
    if prefix.position == 0:
        value = 0.15
    else:
        share = min(1.0, pt_sum / (count + 5.0)) if count else 0.0
        text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
        word = text.strip().lower()
        if word == "para":
            weight = -0.3
        elif word in ARTICLES:
            weight = 1.0
        elif word in WEAK:
            weight = 0.4
        elif text[:1] == " " and word.isalpha():
            weight = 0.7
        elif word.isalpha():
            weight = 0.5
        else:
            weight = 0.2
        value = share * weight
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = text.strip().lower()
    return (doc, pt_sum + looks_portuguese(text, word), count + 1), value

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:5313 — the "open a grouped factor" feature.

What it does: this component fires on the opening bracket of a parenthesised or
bracketed sub-expression in mathematics, most strongly when the bracket comes right
after an arithmetic operator (x / (, a + (, a - (, a * (, a = (), and most of all on
fused forms like "*(" and "/(" where a multiplication or division opens a group.
It is weak after prose words ("if (", "is ("), negative after "for (" (code loops),
and it is scaled by how mathematical the recent text is: in prose or code the same
brackets barely fire. The first token inside a freshly opened group carries a
fraction of the bracket's value. A few dot-leader tokens ("··") also fire.

The program is a set of hand-written rules: which token is an opening bracket, what
came just before it, and how much maths is in the last 12 tokens. It is a
readable approximation, not an exact model of the component.
"""

import re

READS = ()

# Tokens that count as "maths" for the density test: numbers, single letters,
# operators, brackets, LaTeX commands.
MATHY = re.compile(
    r"^\s*(\d+\.?|[a-zA-Z]|[-+*/=^()\[\]×−<>]|\\\\|\*\*|²|left|right|frac|sqrt)\s*$"
)

# Activation for a bracket after a given previous token (stripped).
# Operators are strongest; "/" strongest of all.
PREV_VALUE = {
    "+": 4.5, "-": 4.5, "−": 4.5, "*": 4.5, "×": 4.5, "/": 6.0,
    "=": 2.3, "sqrt": 1.7, "sin": 2.8, "left": 2.5, "(": 1.0, "[": 1.0,
}

# Fused bracket tokens, where the operator and the bracket are one token.
FUSED = {
    "*(": 5.5, "×(": 5.5, "*(-": 6.0, "/(": 2.2,
    ")(": 3.0, ")*(": 4.7, "(-": 1.5, " (-": 4.4,
}

# A closing bracket followed by an operator, as in "(a+b)^2" or "(x)/".
CLOSE_OP = {")^", ")/", ")*", ")+", ")-"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: the value at the previous position (None at a row's start)
    last = 0.0 if carry is None else carry
    toks = prefix.token_strings
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    if len(toks) < 2 or docs[-1] != docs[-2]:
        return 0.0, 0.0  # first token of a document: the model resets here

    # How mathematical the last 12 tokens of this document are, from 0 (prose/code) to 1.
    lo = max(0, len(toks) - 13)
    recent = [toks[i] for i in range(lo, len(toks) - 1) if docs[i] == docs[-1]]
    density = sum(1 for s in recent if MATHY.match(s)) / max(1, len(recent))
    gate = min(1.0, density / 0.6)

    cur = toks[-1].strip()
    prev = toks[-2].strip()
    value = 0.0
    if cur == "··":
        value = 2.0  # run of middle dots, as in leader lines
    elif cur in FUSED:
        value = FUSED[cur] * gate
    elif cur in CLOSE_OP:
        value = 1.0 * gate
    elif "(" in cur or cur in ("left", "["):
        if cur == "left" or prev in PREV_VALUE:
            value = PREV_VALUE.get(prev, 1.8) * gate
        elif prev[-1:].isdigit() or prev[-1:] == ")" or prev[-1:].isalpha():
            value = 0.5 * gate  # e.g. "2(", "f(", ")("
        elif prev in ("for", "foreach"):
            value = -0.5  # loop headers in code
    elif cur in ("*", "×"):
        value = (2.0 if prev[-1:].isdigit() or prev[-1:] == ")" else 0.5) * gate
    elif cur.isalnum() and last >= 1.0:
        value = 0.3 * last  # first token inside a freshly opened group
    return value, value

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:5314 -- a "publication year is coming" detector.

What it does: this component goes strongly negative on the space that comes just
before a publication year in an author-year citation, such as the space in
"(Girard et al., [2005])" or "(Linnaeus, [1758])". At that space the model is about
to write a year, and this component pushes against it. Elsewhere it is near zero,
apart from a weak positive value on the first token of each document.

The program reads only the text so far (the prefix), so it cannot see the year:
it recognises the citation context from the words before the space.

  * space right after "al.," (as in "et al., ")          -> -3.5 (strongest)
  * space right after "al." (as in "et al. ")             -> -1.3
  * space after "Name," inside ( ) or [ ] (e.g. "(Linnaeus, ") -> -1.0
  * space after "Name," elsewhere                         -> -0.5
  * first token of a document (or row)                    -> +0.15
  * everything else                                       -> 0

The values are the mean activations observed in each group on training text.
"""

import re

READS = ()

# A capitalised name, "&"/"and" pair, or "et al.", ending in a comma.
NAME_COMMA = re.compile(r"(et al\.|&\s*[A-Z][\w\-]+|and [A-Z][\w\-]+|[A-Z][\w\-]+),$")

DOC_START = 0.15
ET_AL_COMMA = -3.5
ET_AL = -1.3
CITE_IN_BRACKETS = -1.0
CITE_PLAIN = -0.5


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # first token of a document, or of the row
    if len(prefix.token_ids) == 1 or prefix.token_strings[-2] == "<|endoftext|>":
        return None, DOC_START
    if prefix.token_strings[-1] != " ":
        return None, 0.0
    # the text before this space
    before = prefix.text_prefixes[-1][:-1]
    if before.endswith("al.,"):
        return None, ET_AL_COMMA
    if before.endswith("al."):
        return None, ET_AL
    if not NAME_COMMA.search(before[-40:]):
        return None, 0.0
    if "(" in before[-60:] or "[" in before[-60:]:
        return None, CITE_IN_BRACKETS
    return None, CITE_PLAIN

"""Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:5315, a narrow "th-fragment continuation" detector.

What it does: the component is silent almost everywhere. Its clearest positive
firings come when a word is split into pieces and the piece just before is a bare
"th" fragment (" Th", " th", "th", "TH"), and the current piece is a short lowercase
continuation with no leading space: " Th" + "iam", "th" + "at", "TH" + "AT", the
"t h" + "e" spellings. In those cases it reads roughly 1.0; everywhere else it
predicts 0. Most of its variance (diffuse, signed, moderate values on ordinary text)
is not captured by this rule.
"""

READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if len(prefix) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        return carry, 0.0
    before = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip()
    short_lowercase_piece = token.isascii() and token.isalpha() and token.islower() and len(token) <= 3
    if before.lower() == "th" and short_lowercase_piece:
        return carry, 1.0
    return carry, 0.0

"""A short-fragment detector for the spelling cluster 'dr'.

Large training responses repeatedly occur around this consonant cluster.
The rules detect dr within or across tokens, retain a response in following
word pieces, and allow a few vowel-separated d-r variants. Vowels, length,
and capitalization adjust strength. Transliteration covers other alphabets,
but these rules omit lexical exceptions and many non-Latin spellings.
"""
from functools import lru_cache
from anyascii import anyascii

READS = ()

SPLIT_VOWEL = {
    'a': 0.7,
    'e': 0.1,
    'i': 0.85,
    'o': 1.35,
    'u': 1.95,
    'y': -0.5,
}
FOLLOWING_VOWEL = {
    'a': 1.0,
    'e': 3.2,
    'i': 2.0,
    'o': 1.7,
    'u': 0.75,
    'y': 0.5,
}


@lru_cache(maxsize=16384)
def romanized(text):
    return anyascii(text)


def response(text, previous, before_previous):
    raw = romanized(text)
    t = raw.lower()
    p = romanized(previous).lower()
    q = romanized(before_previous).lower()
    value = 0.0
    at = t.find('dr')
    if at >= 0:
        tail = t[at + 2:]
        capital_d = raw[at].isupper() and not text.isupper()
        value = 1.2 - 0.14 * min(len(tail), 7)
        value += 0.17 * (len(tail) <= 1)
        value += 0.3 * (tail[:1] in ('e', 'i', 'o'))
        value -= 1.1 * (at > 0 and t[at - 1].isalpha() and not capital_d)
        value -= 0.1 * capital_d + 0.36 * text.isupper()
        value -= 0.66 * (text.strip() == 'Dr')
    if p.endswith('d') and t.startswith('r'):
        # Do not mistake a CamelCase word boundary for a consonant cluster.
        if not text[0].isupper() or text.isupper():
            value += 2.25 - 0.2 * min(len(t) - 1, 7)
            value += SPLIT_VOWEL.get(t[1:2], 0.0)
            value += 0.77 * (len(t) == 1) + 2.0 * t.endswith('m')
            value += 1.0 * p.endswith('ud') + 0.2 * (not text.isascii())
    if t and t[0].isalpha() and not text[0].isupper():
        if p.endswith('dr'):
            value += 1.4 - 0.28 * min(len(t), 7)
            value += FOLLOWING_VOWEL.get(t[:1], 0.0)
            value += 0.8 * (len(t) <= 2)
            value -= 0.8 * (not p.lstrip().startswith('dr'))
        elif 'dr' in p or (q.endswith('d') and p.startswith('r')):
            value += 0.8 - 0.15 * min(len(t), 7)
            value += 1.55 * (len(p) <= 2)
        value += 0.44 * (p.endswith('d') and t.startswith('er'))
        value += 0.4 * (p.endswith(('de', 'do', 'du')) and t.startswith('r'))
    return max(0.0, value)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        previous = before_previous = ''
    else:
        _, previous, before_previous = carry
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    return (doc, text, previous), response(text, previous, before_previous)

"""Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:5316 -- the "dr" consonant-cluster detector.

What it responds to: the letters d and r sitting together inside a word, as the
tokenizer splits them. The component is nearly silent everywhere else, and it fires on
the token where a "dr" is completed or begun:

  * a token that starts with r (or Cyrillic р) right after a token ending in d
    (or Cyrillic д), so the cluster is split across two tokens: "ed" + "rops"
    (eyedrops), "octahed" + "ron", "D" + "rom", "Wood" + "row".  Strongest (~3).
  * a word-initial "dr" token: " drive", " dry", " drop", " dress", " dr", "Dr", "dro".
    Medium (~1). "dr" in the middle of a word (address, children, hydro, driver)
    gives almost nothing, so it is not counted.
  * the piece right after a token that ends in "dr": "Dr" + "ives", "dre" + "iß" (~0.8).

Everything else predicts 0. The program is stateless: it reads only the current token
and the previous token of the same document.
"""

READS = ()

STRADDLE = 3.0   # r/р starting a token right after a token ending in d/д
DR_START = 1.0   # a word beginning with "dr" (a leading space is weaker)
DR_AFTER = 0.8   # the token right after one ending in "dr"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    cur = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    same_doc = len(prefix) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2] if same_doc else ""
    lead = cur[:1].isspace()
    head = cur.lstrip()[:1]
    word = cur.lstrip().lower()
    tail = prev[-1:]

    value = 0.0
    if not lead and head and tail and head in "rр" and tail in "dдDД":
        value = STRADDLE
    elif not lead and head and tail and head in "RР" and tail in "DД":
        value = STRADDLE
    elif word.startswith("dr") or word.startswith("др"):
        value = DR_START if not lead else DR_START * 0.8
    elif not lead and prev and ("dr" in prev[-3:].lower() or "др" in prev[-3:].lower()):
        value = DR_AFTER
    return carry, value

"""Approximate a multilingual property/state-noun response.

Use nominalizing endings, whether they attach to an earlier stem, stem
spelling, capitalization, and WordNet noun classes. English corpus frequency
modulates the estimates. On 'of', score the preceding word separately.
Also recognize East Asian property markers and 'statistical significance'.
Some unfinished noun spellings respond if adding y forms a dictionary noun,
or an accented ending makes a common Italian, French, or German word.

Numeric pairs are (whole word, attached fragment); OF_WORD pairs instead mean
(offset, rarity slope). Other positions predict zero. State resets at document
boundaries. These rules capture morphology, not all lexical/contextual variation.
"""
import re
from functools import lru_cache
import wordnet
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

READS = ()

class EndingRule:
    def __init__(self, endings, whole, fragment, after_of=0., last_letter=0.):
        self.endings = tuple(endings.split())
        self.whole, self.fragment = whole, fragment
        self.after_of, self.last_letter = after_of, last_letter


# Spelling families; response on a whole token, on a suffix fragment, and on 'of'.
RULES = {
    'ability': EndingRule(
        'ability abilities ibility ibilities', -0.324, -0.872, -0.896),
    'ality': EndingRule('ality alities', 0.0, -0.963, -0.382),
    'ivity': EndingRule('ivity ivities', -0.232, -0.8, -0.891),
    'arity': EndingRule('arity arities', 0.0, -0.51),
    'ity': EndingRule('ity ities', 0.0, 0.0),
    'ness': EndingRule('ness nesses', 0.0, 0.689, -0.768),
    'ence': EndingRule('ence ance ences ances', 0.0, 0.372),
    'cy': EndingRule('ancy ency acy ancies encies acies', 0.0, 0.273, -0.398),
    'germanic': EndingRule('heit keit heid', -0.261, 0.0),
    'german_ity': EndingRule('ität itäten', 0.0, -1.577, 0.0, -0.792),
    'french': EndingRule('ité ités été etés', 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, -1.376),
    'iberian': EndingRule('idad idades idade dade dades', 0.0, -0.638),
    'italian': EndingRule('ità tà', -0.727, -1.039, 0.0, -2.113),
    'romanian': EndingRule('itate ități ităţii ităţi', 0.0, -1.019),
    'slavic': EndingRule(
        'ность ности ностью ностей ость ости остью остей nost '
        'nosti ność ności сть', 0.0, -0.235),
}

WORD_CLASS = {'cogency': (-2.709, -0.842),
 'connectedness': (-0.52, 0.147),
 'correctness': (-0.372, 0.0),
 'noun.group': (0.0, 0.248),
 'noun.location': (0.0, 0.32),
 'rarity': (-0.082, -0.074),
 'suitability': (-0.515, -0.431),
 'trait': (0.0, 0.21)}

STEM = {'al': -1.551,
 'ic': -1.564,
 'ive': 0.122,
 'ous': -0.256,
 'rarity': -0.125,
 'verb': -0.44}

UPPER = {'ality': 0.345, 'ity': 0.183, 'ness': 2.244}

OF_WORD = {'cogency': (-0.613, -0.797),
 'correctness': (-0.631, -1.016),
 'existence': (-0.405, 0.0),
 'connectedness': (0.0, -0.623),
 'suitability': (0.0, -0.448)}

# Other scalar coefficients.
OF_NOM_RARITY = -0.432
UNFINISHED_OFFSET = -1.628
HAN_NATURE = -0.437
PROPERTY_MEASURE = -0.294
STATISTICAL_SIGNIFICANCE = -2.056

WORD = re.compile(r"[^\W\d_]+$")
KINDS = (set(WORD_CLASS) | set(OF_WORD)) - {'rarity'}


@lru_cache(maxsize=50000)
def family(word):
    for name, rule in RULES.items():
        if word.endswith(rule.endings):
            return name
    return ''


@lru_cache(maxsize=50000)
def facts(word):
    categories = wordnet.categories(word)
    result = {}
    for kind in KINDS:
        result[kind] = float(kind in categories if kind.startswith('noun.')
                             else wordnet.is_a(word, kind))
    result['rarity'] = max(0., 5. - zipf_frequency(word, 'en'))
    return result


@lru_cache(maxsize=50000)
def unfinished(word):
    # A dictionary-supported noun fragment may lack its final letters.
    if (len(word) < 5 or not word.endswith(('it', 'itat', 'ilit', 'abil', 'ibil'))
            or wordnet.parts_of_speech(word)):
        return False
    return ('noun' in wordnet.parts_of_speech(word + 'y') or
            any(zipf_frequency(word + end, language) > 2.
                for end, language in (('à', 'it'), ('é', 'fr'), ('ät', 'de'))))


def predict(token, before):
    previous = WORD.search(before)
    previous = previous.group() if previous else ''
    word = WORD.search(before + token)
    word = word.group().lower() if word else ''
    attached = bool(previous and token and token[0].isalpha())

    if token.lower().strip() == 'of':
        info = facts(previous.lower()) if previous else {}
        rarity = info.get('rarity', 0.)
        name = family(previous.lower())
        value = 0.
        if name:
            value += RULES[name].after_of + OF_NOM_RARITY * rarity
        for kind, (offset, slope) in OF_WORD.items():
            value += (offset + slope * rarity) * info.get(kind, 0.)
        return value

    value = 0.
    name = family(word)
    if name and family(token.strip().lower()):
        info = facts(word)
        value = (RULES[name].whole, RULES[name].fragment)[attached]
        value += sum(pair[attached] * info.get(kind, 0.)
                     for kind, pair in WORD_CLASS.items())
        if token.isupper() and attached and token in ('NESS', 'ITY', 'ITIES'):
            value += UPPER.get(name, 0.)
        if attached:
            stem = previous.lower()
            parts = wordnet.parts_of_speech(stem)
            for feature, weight in STEM.items():
                if feature == 'rarity':
                    value += weight * facts(stem)['rarity']
                elif feature in ('noun', 'verb', 'adjective'):
                    value += weight * (feature in parts)
                else:
                    value += weight * stem.endswith(feature)
    elif attached and len(token.strip()) >= 2 and unfinished(word):
        value = UNFINISHED_OFFSET
    elif previous and token.strip() in ('à', 'é', 'és', 'ät'):
        value = (RULES[name].last_letter if name else 0.)

    if '性' in token:
        value += HAN_NATURE
    if token in ('度', '率', '성'):
        value += PROPERTY_MEASURE
    if (previous.lower() == 'statistical'
            and token.strip().lower() == 'significance'):
        value += STATISTICAL_SIGNIFICANCE
    return value


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    document = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    before = carry[1] if carry and carry[0] == document else ''
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    value = predict(token, before)
    return (document, (before + token)[-100:]), float(value)

"""Derived abstract-noun endings, in several languages, push this component negative.

The component is most negative on the piece that completes a derived abstract noun, when the
noun is split into pieces: -ity in English (periodic|ity, valid|ity, divisibil|ity), -ité in
French, -idad / -idade in Spanish and Portuguese, -ità / -ität in Italian and German,
-ность / -сть in Russian, 性 in Chinese. A word-internal piece (no leading space) whose word so
far ends in such an ending gets -2 when the ending is technical (-ality, -ibility, -ilit, -ität,
-ità, -idad), and -1 otherwise. Whole-word nouns (quality, security) are not flagged, and
neither are -ance or -ness.

The word " of" right after such a word, or after a property noun (stability, accuracy, nature,
presence), gets -1: the component is also negative on "of" there.

The word " magnitude" is reliably about +1. Everything else predicts 0.
"""

READS = ()

# Endings of derived abstract nouns, matched against the word so far.
SUFFIXES = ("ity", "ities", "ité", "ités", "ität", "ità", "idad", "idade", "idades", "keit",
            "heit", "unit", "ilit", "itate", "itat", "ibilidade", "ность", "ности", "ностей",
            "ностью", "ость", "сть", "性")

# The technical endings, the strongest cases.
TECHNICAL = ("ality", "ibility", "ability", "ilit", "itate", "itat", "ität", "ità", "idad",
             "idade", "ibilidade")

# Nouns after which " of" is clearly negative.
PROPERTY_NOUNS = {"existence", "accuracy", "safety", "nature", "presence", "quality",
                  "availability", "possibility", "ability", "behavior", "sensitivity",
                  "stability", "efficiency"}


def word_at(tokens):
    """The letters of the word ending at the last token, lowercased."""
    pieces = []
    for s in reversed(tokens):
        if s.startswith(" "):
            pieces.insert(0, s.strip())
            break
        if not s.isalpha():
            break
        pieces.insert(0, s)
    return "".join(pieces).lower()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tokens = prefix.token_strings
    cur = tokens[-1]
    if cur == " of":
        prev = word_at(tokens[:-1])
        abstract = prev.endswith(("ity", "ty", "cy", "ness", "ence")) or prev in PROPERTY_NOUNS
        return None, (-1.0 if abstract else 0.0)
    word = word_at(tokens)
    if not cur.startswith(" ") and word.endswith(SUFFIXES):
        return None, (-2.0 if word.endswith(TECHNICAL) else -1.0)
    if cur == " magnitude":
        return None, 1.0
    return None, 0.0

"""Layer 1, MLP down-projection, component 5320: the preposition «на» ("on, at, to").

What it does: a strongly negative detector for the Slavic preposition на, as in
"на столе" (on the table) or "надеяться на" (to hope for). It is strongest on the
standalone Cyrillic word на (Russian, Bulgarian, Ukrainian), and on the Latin
spelling "na" when it is a Slavic preposition (Polish, Czech, Slovak text). The
same word in Portuguese ("na cidade" = "in the city") gives roughly zero, so the
program checks whether the document so far contains Cyrillic or Slavic-only
letters. German "auf" ("on, upon") gives a smaller negative value. Weaker
negative values go to the fragments of the same sound: Cyrillic words that
begin with на- (направ-, нап-, наз-), the split "н" + "ав" in "нав-игатор",
and the middle-dot filler "··".

The program predicts the component's activation from the current token, the
previous token and the document's language so far. Negative values mean the
preposition is being read; zero means nothing.
"""

READS = ()

# Polish, Czech and Slovak letters that Portuguese and Spanish do not use.
SLAVIC_LETTERS = set("ąćęłńśźżěřůťďňľĺŕčšž")


def _slavic_text(text):
    """True if the text has a Cyrillic letter or a Slavic-only Latin letter."""
    for c in text:
        if "Ѐ" <= c <= "ӿ" or c.lower() in SLAVIC_LETTERS:
            return True
    return False


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        # A new document: forget the language and the previous token.
        slavic, previous = False, ""
    else:
        _, slavic, previous = carry
    slavic = slavic or _slavic_text(token)
    word = token.strip()
    low = word.lower()

    if token == " на":
        value = -11.0  # the preposition, lowercase, after a space
    elif token in (" На", "На"):
        value = -15.0  # the preposition, capitalised
    elif token == "на":
        value = -0.6  # the same letters glued to a previous piece
    elif token in (" na", " Na", "Na"):
        value = -10.0 if slavic else 0.0  # Latin spelling, Slavic text only
    elif low == "auf":
        value = -3.5  # German "auf"
    elif low == "uf":
        value = -1.2  # "auf" split across tokens, as in "Wiederau-fnahme"
    elif token == "ав" and previous.strip() in ("н", "Н"):
        value = -10.0  # "н" + "ав" spells "на" across two tokens
    elif word[:2].lower() == "на" and len(word) > 2:
        value = -1.0  # other words starting with на- (направ-, нап-, наз-)
    elif token == "··":
        value = -1.3  # middle-dot filler token
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return (doc, slavic, token), value

"""Candidate v5: the resultative 到 that means 'reach / attain / perceive / be affected by'
(看到, 找到, 学到, 买到, 感受到, 影响到, 用到), plus the 'to' after 'learn'.

The component is pushed negative on the 到 (or 了-suffixed 到了) that ends a verb of getting,
perceiving or being affected, and pushed positive on the 'to' of 'learn to'. Everywhere else
it predicts 0. This is a hand-written rule, not a fitted table."""

READS = ()

# verbs (their last character) that take 到 as a result complement
ATTAIN_VERBS = set("看找得见收抓买拿吃学感受遇碰接想识获取不用害谈扯影帮")
RESULT_NEG = -2.0       # mean activation on such 到 is about -1.5 to -2.5
LEARN_TO = 2.4          # the 'to' after learn/learned/learning: mean about +2.6
LEARN_WORDS = ("learn", "learns", "learned", "learnt", "learning")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    text = prefix.text_prefixes[-1]
    stem = text[:-1] if text.endswith("了") else text    # 到了 counts as 到
    if stem.endswith("到") and len(stem) > 1 and stem[-2] in ATTAIN_VERBS:
        return None, RESULT_NEG
    if prefix.token_strings[-1] == " to":
        words = text[:-3].split()
        if words and words[-1].lower() in LEARN_WORDS:
            return None, LEARN_TO
    return None, 0.0

"""An orthographic MOR/MUR-fragment detector, not a semantic topic detector.

Look for m-or, m-ur and m-our, including spellings split between subwords.
The response is strongest at a fragment's end; extra suffix letters and
familiar complete words usually weaken it. An attached next subword gets a
smaller echo. Transliteration lets the same rules cover some other scripts.
The few numerical adjustments are calibrated on training text.
"""
import re
from functools import lru_cache
from anyascii import anyascii
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

READS = ()

@lru_cache(maxsize=50000)
def spelling(text):
    return anyascii(text).lower()

@lru_cache(maxsize=50000)
def frequency(word):
    return zipf_frequency(word, 'en')


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    first = carry is None or carry[0] != doc
    previous, word = ('', '') if first else carry[1:]
    s = spelling(text)
    token = s.strip()
    attached = bool(s and s[0].isalpha() and previous
                    and previous[-1].isalpha())
    old = word if attached else ''
    word = old + token if token.isalpha() else ''
    if not word:
        tail = re.search(r'[a-z]+$', token)
        word = tail.group() if tail else ''
    value = 0.0

    # Fragment contained in the current token.
    match = re.search(r'm(?:o|ou|u)r', token)
    if match and frequency(word or token) <= 4.8:
        suffix = token[match.end():]
        n = len(suffix)
        value = (4.3, 1.5, 1.7, 2.3, 1.2, 0.3)[min(n, 5)]
        value -= 1.1 * max(0, frequency(word or token) - 3.5)
        value -= 1.1 * (match.group() == 'mur')
        value -= 0.9 * (match.group() == 'mour')
        value += 1.4 * suffix.startswith('ph')
        value += 0.3 * ('r' in suffix)
        value += 0.3 * attached
        value += 3.2 * first
        if match.start():
            before = token[match.start() - 1]
            value -= 0.8
            value += {'a': 0.9, 'e': -0.3, 'o': 2.0,
                      'r': 0.6, 'u': -2.1}.get(before, 0)

    # Fragment completed across attached subwords.
    cross = re.match(r'(or|ur|our)', token) if attached else None
    if cross and old.endswith('m'):
        vowel = cross.group()
        value += {'or': 6.0, 'ur': 4.2, 'our': 2.8}[vowel]
        before = old[-2:-1]
        value += {'a': 2.8, 'e': 2.0, 'i': 2.2,
                  'r': 2.8, 'u': -0.3}.get(before, 0)
        value -= 0.5 * (len(old) == 1)
        value -= 0.3 * (len(previous.strip()) <= 1)
        value -= 0.3 * (len(old) > 3)
        value += 5.8 * token.startswith('orph')
        value -= 1.2 * min(len(token) - len(vowel), 5)
    elif cross and re.search(r'm[a-z]{1,2}$', old):
        value += 0.2 + 2.6 * old.endswith('me')
    elif attached and token.startswith('r'):
        value += 0.3 * bool(re.search(r'm[aeiou]{1,2}$', old))

    # A smaller response can persist into the next suffix.
    if attached and re.search(r'm(?:o|ou|u)r$', previous):
        if not text.isupper() and frequency(word) <= 4.8:
            value += 2.2 + 0.6 * max(0, frequency(word) - 3)
            value += 2.7 * token.startswith(('f', 'ph'))
            value -= 2.2 * (len(token) > 4)
    elif attached and re.search(r'm(?:o|ou|u)r.{1,3}$', previous):
        value += 0.2
    return (doc, s, word[-40:]), max(0.0, value)

"""Fires on the letters m-o-r / m-u-r when they are spelled inside a word.

Concept: the component responds to the spelling "mor" / "mur" (and close
spellings "mour", "maur", "meur") split across word pieces, e.g. the piece
"mor" in "Armor" or "al|mor|zar", the piece "or" in "nam|or|ados" or
"Am|or", the piece "urt" in "Dakshinam|urt|i" or "ur" in "Tim|ur".

The program follows the letters of the current word (letters since the last
non-letter character; reset at each new document). On the token that first
completes one of those spellings in the word, it fires. It fires harder when
that token is a short piece (1-3 letters, e.g. "mor", "or", "ur"), less when it
is a longer token (e.g. "Armor", "morph"), and weakly on later pieces of the same
word (morse -> "se", lagamorphs -> "s"). Whole common words that contain the
letters (more, memory, morning, tumor, order) stay quiet.
"""

READS = ()
KEYS = ("mor", "mur", "mour", "meur", "maur")
QUIET = {"more", "moreover", "furthermore", "anymore", "memory", "morning",
         "tumor", "murder", "mortgage", "mortality", "order"}
SHORT = 4.0
LONG = 2.0
CONT = 1.3


def has_key(text):
    return any(k in text for k in KEYS)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word, doc = carry if carry is not None else ("", None)
    if prefix.document_ids[-1] != doc:
        word = ""
    start = word
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    for ch in s.lower():
        word = (word + ch)[-8:] if (ch.isascii() and ch.isalpha()) else ""
    hit = has_key(word) and word not in QUIET
    if not hit:
        value = 0.0
    elif has_key(start):
        value = CONT
    elif len(s.strip()) <= 3:
        value = SHORT
    else:
        value = LONG
    return (word, prefix.document_ids[-1]), value

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:5323: a near-silent component with two readable triggers.

What it does, in plain terms:
1. Start of a text. On the first token of a document (the first token of a row, or the
   token right after <|endoftext|>), it is pushed negative on average, about -0.15. Nothing
   comes before that token, so the value depends only on which token it is; individual
   tokens range from about -3 to +2, and this rule predicts the average.
2. The digit pair "30" or "31". A "0" or "1" directly after a "3" (as in "September 30",
   "1930", "31 days") is pushed negative: about -0.42 after "3" then "0", about -0.20 after
   "3" then "1".

Everywhere else it sits near zero, with small token-specific wiggles (about +/-0.05) that
no simple rule captures. Activations are nearly uncorrelated from one position to the next,
so there is no slow context feature to describe.

Main program: the two rules, applied token by token, with no state carried between tokens.
What the simple version gets: about 5% of the activation's variance on eval rows, and it
leaves the model's next-token predictions essentially unchanged (its e2e effect is close to
switching the component off). A per-token table would add the many rare token-pair effects
and reach a much higher in-sample fit, but those are arbitrary token ids, so it is not
included.
"""

READS = ()

DOC_START = -0.15
AFTER_THREE = {"0": -0.42, "1": -0.20}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        return None, DOC_START
    if prefix.token_strings[-2] == "3" and token in AFTER_THREE:
        return None, AFTER_THREE[token]
    return None, 0.0

"""Layer-1 MLP down-projection component 5325, as a token-level program.

It is nearly silent everywhere. It fires strongly on two kinds of text:
  * the token "··" (two middle dots, U+00B7), in runs of decorative dots:
    activation about 3.2;
  * the NUL byte "\\x00", which appears between the letters of spaced-out or
    UTF-16-like text: about 1.5 after a letter, about 0.5 after a space.
Everywhere else it predicts 0.
"""

READS = ()

MIDDLE_DOTS = "··"
NUL = "\x00"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if tok == MIDDLE_DOTS:
        return None, 3.2
    if tok == NUL:
        before = prefix.token_strings[-2] if len(prefix) > 1 else ""
        return None, 0.5 if before == " " else 1.5
    return None, 0.0

"""Layer 1, MLP down-projection, component 5326.

Almost always near zero. Its size is set mostly by the token itself and, where it is
large, by the start of a document. Three rare, recognisable triggers and one weak
document-start rule:

1. The colon of a "Title:" header at the very start of a document: -3.2
   (its most negative value; the measured value is about -3.16).
2. The two-dot leader token "··": +1.2.
3. "dro" right after "Hy" (as in "Hydro..."): +2.1.
4. The first token of a document, which the component reads without context:
   a capitalised word +0.07, a digit -0.08, a lowercase word -0.04; anything else 0.

Everywhere else it predicts 0. Most of its variance is diffuse, token-specific noise with
no readable concept, so this program explains only a few percent of it.
"""

READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    cur = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2] if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 else ""
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    t = prefix.position
    starts_doc = t == 0 or docs[-1] != docs[-2]
    if cur == ":" and prev == "Title" and (t == 1 or docs[-3] != docs[-2]):
        return carry, -3.2
    if cur == "··":
        return carry, 1.2
    if cur == "dro" and prev == "Hy":
        return carry, 2.1
    if starts_doc and cur.strip():
        if cur[0].isupper():
            return carry, 0.07
        if cur[0].isdigit():
            return carry, -0.08
        if cur[0].isalpha():
            return carry, -0.04
    return carry, 0.0

"""Layer 1 MLP down_proj component 5327: a document-start "Title:" detector, plus the
small typical offset of the first token of each document.

Most of this component's variance is small, diffuse noise (about 0.04 in size) with no
simple token or position pattern, so this program predicts its mean there. Its one large,
clean response is a colon that directly follows a document's first token "Title", as in
the headline "Title: ..." opening many web-scraped documents: there it jumps to about 6.8.
A document starts after each <|endoftext|> token (the model resets attention there); the
first token of a document averages about -0.15 in this component.
"""

READS = ()

TITLE_COLON_ACTIVATION = 6.75
FIRST_TOKEN_MEAN = -0.15


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry["doc"] != doc:
        index, previous = 0, None  # first token of a new document
    else:
        index, previous = carry["index"] + 1, carry["token"]
    value = 0.0
    if index == 0:
        value = FIRST_TOKEN_MEAN
    elif index == 1 and previous == "Title" and token == ":":
        value = TITLE_COLON_ACTIVATION
    return {"doc": doc, "index": index, "token": token}, value

"""Concession and "not only" contrast words, as the component's activation.

Layer 1, MLP down-projection, component 5328. It is silent almost everywhere, but it
goes strongly negative on the word that opens a concession or a "not only" contrast:

  * the "only" of "not only" (also Russian "не только", Italian "non solo",
    French "non seulement", Dutch "niet alleen", Polish "nie tylko"): about -6 to -9,
    the largest values there are;
  * concessive "although" in Chinese (虽然, 雖然, 尽管, 儘管), Vietnamese "tuy",
    Romanian "totuși": about -5 to -10;
  * the "though" of "even though" (about -4), and bare "although" (about -1.3) and
    "though" (about -0.6);
  * weaker: "if" after "even", "just" after "not", sentence-initial "While".

Everything else, including ordinary "only", "but", "however", "despite", is about 0.
The program looks only at the last three tokens of the current document, so it keeps
no state between positions.
"""

READS = ()

# (text ending at this token, lowercased) -> predicted activation
PHRASES = [
    ("not only", -6.5), ("не только", -6.5), ("non solo", -9.0), ("no solo", -6.0),
    ("non seulement", -8.0), ("pas seulement", -6.0), ("niet alleen", -4.0),
    ("nie tylko", -4.0), ("nicht nur", -2.0),
    ("even though", -4.2), ("even if", -0.8), ("not just", -1.0),
    ("tuy", -10.0), ("totuși", -4.0), ("zwar", -2.8),
    ("although", -1.3), ("though", -0.6),
]
# Chinese words are written without spaces, so a token may hold part of a longer word.
CHINESE = {"虽": -8.5, "雖": -8.0, "尽管": -6.0, "儘管": -8.0, "即使": -1.4,
           "即便": -1.1, "不但": -2.8, "不仅": -0.9}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    n = len(prefix)
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    k = 1
    while k < 3 and k < n and docs[-1 - k] == docs[-1]:
        k += 1
    tokens = prefix.token_strings[n - k:]
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    text = "".join(tokens).lower()
    for word, value in CHINESE.items():
        if word in tok:
            return carry, value
    for phrase, value in PHRASES:
        if text.endswith(phrase):
            return carry, value
    if tok in ("While", " While") and k > 1:
        if tokens[-2].rstrip(" ")[-1:] in (".", "\n", "!", "?"):
            return carry, -0.85
    return carry, 0.0

"""Detect newly completed spellings of 'plug' and a few related blockage words.

A token completing 'plug' gets a large positive response, even if the word
was split across tokens. Software 'plugin' tokens are weaker. Clog, plough,
and Chinese insertion/blockage characters get smaller positive responses.
Unfinished p-l spellings give a small negative signal; abbreviated 'pls'
and 'plz' give a stronger one. Other tokens are near zero.
"""
import re

READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        tail, previous, last_plug = '', '', False
    else:
        _, tail, previous, last_plug = carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    lower = token.lower()
    text = tail + lower
    boundary = len(tail)
    value = 0.0
    is_plug = False

    # A completed root fires once, not on every later suffix token.
    for root, strength in [('plug', 10.0), ('clog', 6.0),
                           ('plough', 2.4), ('plow', 2.4)]:
        i = text.rfind(root)
        if i >= 0 and i + len(root) > boundary:
            value = strength
            if root == 'plug':
                is_plug = True
                if 'plugin' in lower:
                    value = 0.8
                elif lower.endswith(('plugs', 'plugged')):
                    value = 12.0
                elif token.startswith(' Plug'):
                    value = 12.5
                elif token.startswith('Plug'):
                    value = 9.0
            elif root == 'clog' and text.endswith('unclog'):
                value = 9.0
            break

    if not value:
        word = token.strip()
        if word == '插':  # insert / plug in
            value = 4.0
        elif word == '堵':  # block / plug up
            value = 7.4
        elif word == '塞':  # stuff / stopper
            value = 2.8
        elif '插' in word:
            value = 0.5
        elif last_plug and lower.strip() in {'in', 'it'}:
            value = 1.6
        elif lower and not lower[0].isspace():
            if previous.endswith('pl') and lower[0].isalpha():
                value = -0.4
                if lower == 's':  # pls: abbreviated 'please', also PLS acronyms
                    value = -6.5
                elif lower == 'z':  # plz: another abbreviation of 'please'
                    value = -3.7
            elif previous.endswith('p') and lower.startswith('l'):
                value = 0.5 if re.match(r'l[aeiou]*g', lower) else -0.3
    return (doc, text[-24:], lower, is_plug), value

"""Fires on the word "plug" and its forms, and on the Chinese words 插, 堵, 塞 (insert, block).

The component writes a large push into the residual stream on the token that completes a
"plug" word: " plug", "Plug", " plugs", " plugged", "unplug", or the second half of a word
split as "pl" + "ugging" / "pl" + "uggy". It is near zero on "pl" itself and on almost every
other token; "plough"/"plow" give a weaker response.
"""

import re

READS = ()

PLUG_WORD = re.compile(r"plugg?(s|ed|ing|y)?$")
PLOUGH_WORD = re.compile(r"plo(ugh|w)(s|ed|ing)?$")
CHINESE_PLUG = {"插": 4.0, "堵": 7.5, "塞": 2.8}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: (the lowercase letters of the current word so far, the document it belongs to)
    word, doc = carry if carry is not None else ("", None)
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if prefix.document_ids[-1] != doc:
        word = ""
    if not (token[:1].isascii() and token[:1].isalpha()):
        word = ""
    word += re.search(r"[A-Za-z]*$", token).group().lower()
    value = CHINESE_PLUG.get(token, 0.0)
    if PLUG_WORD.search(word):
        value = 10.0
    elif PLOUGH_WORD.search(word):
        value = 3.0
    return (word, prefix.document_ids[-1]), value

"""Approximate a multilingual spelling/sound feature, strongest on Japanese long i.

A token beginning with the Japanese length mark is negative, especially after
an i-vowel kana and when the next kana is not yet fully decoded. The effect
continues briefly into the following kana. Smaller responses cover short
Cyrillic i/ri fragments after consonants (stronger at word/name starts)
and repeated middle dots.
These are spelling rules, not a general pronunciation model.
"""
import unicodedata
from anyascii import anyascii

READS = ()
CYRILLIC_CONSONANTS = frozenset('бвгджзйклмнпрстфхцчшщ')
VOICED_KANA_STOPS = frozenset('ガギグゲゴダヂヅデドバビブベボ')


def kana_vowel(char):
    name = unicodedata.name(char, '')
    if not name.startswith(('KATAKANA LETTER', 'HIRAGANA LETTER')):
        return ''
    if char in 'ッっンん':
        return ''
    reading = anyascii(char).lower()
    return reading[-1:] if reading[-1:] in ('a', 'i', 'u', 'e', 'o') else ''


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, b'', '', '', 0)
    _, recent, previous, long_vowel, phase = carry
    b = prefix.token_bytes[-1]
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    before = recent.decode('utf-8', 'replace')[-1:]
    value = 0.0
    next_vowel, next_phase = '', 0

            value = {'i': -7.5, 'u': -3.5, 'o': -2.1,
                     'e': -1.2, 'a': 0.2}.get(vowel, 0.0)
        else:
            value = {'i': -3.5, 'u': -1.1, 'o': -0.6,
                     'e': -0.3, 'a': 0.1}.get(vowel, 0.0)

                value = -7.5

    elif phase:

        continuation = bool(b) and 0x80 <= b[0] < 0xc0
        kana = bool(token) and 'KATAKANA' in unicodedata.name(token[0], '')
        if continuation or kana:
            value = {'i': -2.8 if continuation else -0.8,
                     'u': -1.0 if continuation else -0.4,
                     'o': -0.5 if continuation else -0.2,
                     'e': -0.5 if continuation else -0.2}.get(long_vowel, 0.0)
            if phase == 2:
                value *= 0.5
            if continuation and phase == 1:
                next_vowel, next_phase = long_vowel, 2

Katakana spells most foreign words, and many of them are split into several tokens.
This component goes negative on a katakana token that continues a katakana word (the
token before it is katakana too, with no space in between), and most strongly when the
token is a long-vowel mark ー that extends the word: スピー|ー, ビー|ー, チー|ク, フィード|バック.
Everywhere else it stays near zero.

The program predicts those values: -1.3 on a long-vowel mark that continues a katakana
word, -0.2 on other katakana continuation pieces, -0.4 on a long-vowel mark after a
non-katakana token, and 0 elsewhere.

LONG_VOWEL = "ー"

    """True if the text holds a katakana character or the long-vowel mark."""
    return any("KATAKANA" in unicodedata.name(c, "") or c == LONG_VOWEL for c in text)

    t = prefix.position
    token = prefix.token_strings[t]
    continues = t > 0 and prefix.document_ids[t - 1] == prefix.document_ids[t] and not token.startswith(" ")

        return carry, 0.0

  the "A" of "%3A" (:), the "0" of "%20" (space), the "D" of "%3D" (=).
  On the first digit "2" right after a "%" it is weakly positive (about +2.5).
- Dot leaders (runs of middle dots) are negative (about -1.2).
- The first token of each document is slightly negative (about -0.2), and the
  colon of a "Title:" header that opens a document is strongly negative (about -5.6).
- Zero elsewhere. Most of the component's variance is small, diffuse, token-specific
  noise that this program does not describe.

ESCAPE_FIRST_2 = 2.5  # the "2" that opens an escape such as %2F or %20
DOC_START = -0.2
TITLE_COLON = -5.6
DOT_LEADER = -1.2

PUNCT = set(string.punctuation + " ")


def _punct_escape(first, second):
    """True if the hex pair first+second is the code of an ASCII punctuation mark or space."""

    strs = prefix.token_strings
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]

    prev2 = strs[-3] if len(strs) >= 3 else ""

on kh joins, and on nearby continuations. Cyrillic kha, Greek chi,

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tokens, docs = prefix.token_strings, prefix.document_ids

    prev = tokens[-2] if len(tokens) > 1 and docs[-2] == docs[-1] else ''
    before = tokens[-3] if len(tokens) > 2 and docs[-3] == docs[-1] else ''
    s, p, q = raw.lower(), prev.lower(), before.lower()
    word, previous = s.strip(), p.strip()
    letter = s[:1].isalpha()
    digit = s[:1].isdigit()
    joined = bool(s) and not s[0].isspace()
    value = 0.0005

    # Latin x: continuations, indices, and powers.
    if p.endswith('x'):
        if letter:
            value -= 0.24
            value -= 0.31 * (previous == 'x')
            value += 0.30 * p.endswith('ex')
            value += 0.47 * p.endswith('-ex')
            value += 3.32 * s.startswith('ide')  # oxide / hydroxide

        value -= 0.21

    if p.endswith('kh') and letter:

        value -= 2.46 * prev.endswith(('Kh', 'KH'))

    if 'خ' in s:

When a capitalised word is split into exactly two tokens and the second token is a
word-internal fragment (no leading space, starts with a letter), e.g. 'K|hat', 'Tax|on',
'Pax|ton', 'Rak|hi', the component is pushed slightly negative. Everywhere else it is 0.

This is a deliberately small program. It captures the direction of the component's largest
responses (the strongest activations, down to about -5, occur on such second pieces), but its
magnitude is tiny because most such fragments are near zero; on random text it has almost no
predictive power (see the explanation).

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    toks = prefix.token_strings
    cur = toks[-1]

        return None, 0.0

    start = len(toks) - 1

        start -= 1

What it does, in plain terms:
- Strongly negative (about -6) on the English word "wet", as a whole word or spelt out over
  tokens: the value sits on the token that completes the word, so "W" + "et" fires on "et"
  and "wet" + "ting" fires on "wet" (and "ting" as well). It also fires on a few words that
  sound like it: "wetting", "wetter", "wets", "wett", "wick", "wicked", "wicket", "swet",
  "wex". The Chinese words 湿 and 濕 (wet) give about -7.
- Strongly positive (about +10) on "that" directly after "now" ("now that", meaning "since"
  or "given that").
- Everything else is near zero. Translations of "wet" in French, German, Spanish, Polish,
  Russian, Japanese and Korean do not fire it.

previous token. It needs no other component.

WET_WORDS = {"wet", "wets", "wett", "wetting", "wetter", "wick", "wicked", "wicket", "swet", "wex"}
WET_CHARS = {"湿": -7.0, "濕": -7.0}  # Chinese for "wet"
WET_VALUE = -6.0

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: (word spelt so far in this document, previous token's bare text, document id)
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]

    if word and tok[:1].isalpha():

    elif word in WET_WORDS:
        value = WET_VALUE
    elif bare == "that" and prev == "now":
        value = NOW_THAT_VALUE
    return (word, bare, doc), float(value)

- The first token of each document (the token right after a document break, where attention
  can see nothing else) gets a steady value fixed by what kind of token it is. Numbers and
  ordinary capitalized words are negative, a leading-space word is less negative, and a few
  code/markdown openers are strongly positive ("using", "**", "export", "#") or negative ("//").

  negative value the component ever takes (about -2.85).
- A "###" heading that follows a bare blank line is negative (about -0.4 on average).
- The blank line right after an empty chat think block, "</think>\n\n", is slightly positive.
- A carriage return "\r" is slightly positive.
- Everywhere else the component is small noise (about +/-0.05) spread over the whole vocabulary;
  this program predicts 0 there.

plus the few contexts above, are the parts that a short rule set can state. Most of the
remaining variance is small, token-specific noise with no simple concept behind it.
"""

START_BY_KIND = {"digit": -0.44, "capital": -0.40, "lower": -0.31, "space_word": -0.18, "other": -0.2}
START_EXCEPTIONS = {"using": 1.9, "#": 0.5, "//": -1.45, "**": 2.5, "export": 2.5}


def kind(s):
    """A coarse kind of token: a number, a word with a leading space, a capitalized or
    lowercase word, or anything else (punctuation, code, newlines)."""

    if s[:1] == " " and s[1:].isalpha():

"""A coarse English noun-phrase detector using dictionary word classes.

Score noun candidates by word length, preceding noun/adjective chains, and
preceding-word frequency. Hyphenated modifiers count by their parts. These
rules approximate the observed positive signal around modified nouns, not a
full syntactic parse. Join split words in a bounded rolling buffer. Document
starts receive a negative offset, larger for a capitalized English word.
Lexical idiosyncrasies and non-English effects are not modeled.

from functools import lru_cache

from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

    their each every any some no another such which what whose'''.split())
FUNCTION = set('''of in on at by for from with to into onto about over under
    through between as than and or but if so because while when where who whom
    whose which that is are was were be been being am do does did have has had
    can could will would shall should may might must not it he she they we i
    you'''.split())

TAIL = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z]+(?:[-'][A-Za-z]+)*$")
PREVIOUS = re.compile(r"([A-Za-z]+(?:[-'][A-Za-z]+)*)[ \t]+$")

@lru_cache(maxsize=50000)
def parts(word):
    return wordnet.parts_of_speech(word.lower())


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    first = carry is None or carry[0] != doc
    text = '' if first else carry[1]
    text = (text + prefix.token_strings[-1])[-180:]

    word = tail.group().lower() if tail else ''

        return carry, -0.699 if upper else -0.376

    pos = parts(word)

    for item in reversed(WORDS.findall(before)):
        w = item.lower()

            break
        if not parts(w) & {'noun', 'adjective'}:
            break
        chain += 1 + w.count('-')

    previous = match.group(1).lower() if match else ''

        return carry, 0.013
    noun_only = not pos & {'adjective', 'verb', 'adverb'}
    rare_modifier = zipf_frequency(previous, 'en') < 3
    return carry, 0.188 if noun_only and rare_modifier else 0.046

"""A lexical approximation: continuity, affiliation, regions, and flow in CJK.

Standalone characters respond much more strongly than most compounds. It
also includes opposite-sign lexical responses and document-opening biases.
UTF-8 fragments are joined before testing.
This is a lexical approximation, not a general semantic classifier.
"""
from functools import lru_cache
import opencc
import codecs

READS = ()
_SIMPLIFY = opencc.OpenCC('t2s')


@lru_cache(maxsize=32768)
def lexical_value(text):
    word = text.strip()
    simple = _SIMPLIFY.convert(word)

    # Region/domain, affiliation, continuation, and outflow morphemes.
    if simple == '域':
        return 4.9
    if simple == '属':
        return 5.0 if word == '屬' else 3.7
    if simple == '续' or word == '続':
        return 2.2 if word == '続' else (3.8 if word == '續' else 3.5)
    if simple in ('泻', '泄', '洩'):
        return 3.8
    if word == '속':  # Korean: inside, affiliation, succession, speed.
        return 3.0
    if word == '継':
        return 1.5
    if word in ('繋', '繫'):
        return 1.8 if word == '繋' else 0.7
    if simple in ('系', '族'):
        return 0.7
    if simple == '辖':  # jurisdiction
        return 2.6
    if simple == '序':  # sequence/order
        return 0.85
    if simple == '脉':  # vein, pulse, or lineage
        return 3.7 if word == '脈' else 3.2

    # Common Chinese compounds for belonging and continuation.
    if simple in ('属于', '隶属于', '直属', '所属', '归属'):
        return 2.6
    if simple == '属性':  # attribute/property
        return 0.6
    if simple == '下属':  # subordinate
        return 2.0
    if simple == '专属':  # exclusive affiliation
        return 1.8
    if simple in ('家属', '金属'):  # relatives; metal
        return 0.4
    if simple in ('持续', '后续'):  # persistence; follow-up
        return 2.0 if word == '持續' else 2.6
    if simple == '陆续':  # in succession
        return 1.4
    if simple == '延续':  # extending/continuing
        return 1.0
    if simple == '继续':  # keep doing
        return 0.7
    if simple == '连续':  # consecutive
        return 0.3
    if simple == '区域':  # area/region
        return 2.7 if word == '區域' else 1.1
    if simple == '地域':  # geographical region
        return 0.6
    if simple == '系列':  # series
        return 0.45

    # Opposite-signed lexical responses, not a language-independent meaning.
    if word == '繰':  # winding/reeling, often in Japanese "repeat"
        return -2.1
    if word == '綺':  # fine patterned silk; Japanese "beautiful"
        return -2.6
    if simple == '阵':  # formation; a spell of activity
        return -1.7
    lower = word.lower()
    if lower.startswith('continu'):
        return -0.26
    if lower.startswith('belong'):
        return -0.18
    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        tail, first, count = b'', '', 0
    else:
        _, tail, first, count = carry
    newest = prefix.token_bytes[-1]
    # Keep only unfinished UTF-8 bytes, so a split character is tested once.
    data = tail + newest
    text, consumed = codecs.utf_8_decode(data, 'ignore', False)
    pending = data[consumed:]
    value = lexical_value(text)
    if count == 0:
        first = text
        if text == '//\n':
            value = -4.48
        elif value == 0.0:
            # At document openings, spelling and token shape have larger biases.
            word = text.strip()
            if word.isascii() and word:
                if word.startswith('.') and word[1:2].isalpha():
                    value = -0.47  # a dotted field/member access
                elif word.isalpha() and word.isupper():
                    value = 0.18
                elif word.isdigit():
                    value = 0.10
                elif not any(ch.isalnum() for ch in word):
                    value = -0.10
                elif word.isalpha() and word.islower():
                    value = 0.07 if text[:1].isspace() else -0.04
    if count == 1 and first == '1' and text == '2':
        value = 3.8
    if count == 1 and first == 'Title' and text == ':':
        value = -2.06
    if first == '\r':
        if text == '\r':
            value = -2.0
        else:
            first = ''
    return (doc, pending, first, count + 1), value

"""Feeling-sense detector (negative).

The component switches on (negative) at the word "sense" in its feeling sense
("a sense of home"), at the "of" that follows a feeling noun ("a sense of",
"a feeling of", "the air of"), and at the bare word for sense or feeling in
Chinese, Korean and Vietnamese (感, 감, cảm). Its strongest response is the
"of" after "sense". It is weaker on "of" after other figurative nouns
("a shade of", "a hint of") and on the Chinese 减 / 減 (reduce). It is near
zero everywhere else, including "make sense" and "in the sense that".
"""
from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# Activation on " of" after a feeling noun.
OF_AFTER_FEELING = {"sense": -10.0, "senses": -6.5, "feeling": -6.0, "feelings": -6.0,
                    "air": -3.7, "sensation": -1.8, "touch": -1.9, "perception": -1.9}
# Other figurative nouns that take "of": weakly negative.
OF_AFTER_FIGURATIVE = {"layer", "layers", "shade", "shades", "glimpse", "hint",
                       "impression", "wave", "spark", "blend", "mix", "view", "grasp",
                       "trace", "taste"}
# "sense" after these is a verb ("make sense") or "in the sense": neutral.
NOT_NOUN_SENSE = {"the", "this", "that", "in", "make", "makes", "made", "no", "can", "to"}
MAKE_WORDS = {"make", "makes", "made", "making"}
FEELING_WORD = {"感", "감", "cảm"}  # bare "sense, feeling" word
REDUCE_WORD = {"减", "減"}  # "reduce", weaker


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    # Look back three tokens, but only within the current document.
    toks = [s.strip() for s in prefix.token_strings[-3:]]
    docs = prefix.document_ids[-3:]
    word = toks[-1]
    prev = toks[-2].lower() if len(toks) > 1 and docs[-2] == docs[-1] else ""
    prev2 = toks[-3].lower() if len(toks) > 2 and docs[-3] == docs[-1] else ""

    if word == "of":
        if prev == "sense" and prev2 in MAKE_WORDS:  # "make sense of"
            return carry, 0.0
        if prev == "sense" and prev2 == "the":  # "the sense of"
            return carry, -6.0
        if prev in OF_AFTER_FEELING:
            return carry, OF_AFTER_FEELING[prev]
        return carry, (-1.5 if prev in OF_AFTER_FIGURATIVE else 0.0)
    if word.lower() == "sense":
        return carry, 0.0 if prev in NOT_NOUN_SENSE else -3.5
    if word in FEELING_WORD:
        return carry, -6.0
    if word in REDUCE_WORD:
        return carry, -3.5
    if word.endswith("感"):  # compounds: 性感, 情感, 安全感
        return carry, -3.5
    return carry, 0.0

"""Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:5346, a word-level detector.

Its activation is strongly negative on the opening word of a "no matter whether"
concessive clause (不管, 无论, 不论是, 無論), moderately negative on "don't know /
exactly / after all" words (不知, 不知道, 到底, 究竟, 其实), on 管 in its
"mind / take care of" sense, on 论/論 (argue, thesis), and weakly negative on the
English "whether". It is positive on "finally / in the end" words (最后, 最後, 最终,
最終, 最后一, 到最后). Every other token gets 0, which is most of the time.

The program is a lookup from those word classes to fixed values. It keeps no state
and ignores the context, because the component's sign and size are set by the word.
"""
READS = ()

# Concessive "no matter whether / whatever" openers: the strongest response.
NO_MATTER = {"无论", "无论是", "不管", "不管是", "不论", "不论是", "無論", "無論是"}
# "Don't know", "exactly", "after all": a moderate negative response.
DOUBT = {"不知", "不知道", "到底", "究竟"}
AFTER_ALL = {"其实", "其實"}
# 管 meaning "mind / take care of", and 论 / 論 (argue, thesis).
MANAGE = {"管"}
DEBATE = {"论", "論", "辩论", "辯論"}
# English "whether": weak.
WHETHER = {"whether", "Whether"}
# "Finally / in the end": positive.
FINALLY = {"最后", "最後", "最终", "最終", "最后一", "到最后"}

VALUES = [
    (NO_MATTER, -7.5),
    (MANAGE, -3.5),
    (DOUBT, -1.6),
    (AFTER_ALL, -1.0),
    (DEBATE, -1.2),
    (WHETHER, -0.5),
    (FINALLY, 1.5),
]


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip()
    for words, value in VALUES:
        if tok in words:
            return carry, value
    return carry, 0.0

"""Approximate a short-range noun-phrase/postmodifier signal.

Recent 'the' strengthens negative responses to relative pronouns, relative
clause subjects, spatial/temporal modifiers and participles. Quantifiers,
s-ending heads and dictionary noun classes supply weaker related cues.
This is a decaying grammatical heuristic, not a full syntactic parser.
Articles have a separate continuation response. Clause markers reset
article memory; other words and within-word token fragments predict zero.
"""
import re
from functools import lru_cache
import wordnet

READS = ()

# Grammatical families: baseline and sensitivity to the noun-phrase cue.
RESPONSES = (
    ('that', -.053, .696),
    ('which', -.274, .634),
    ('who whom', -.299, 1.034),
    ('where', -.023, .613),
    ('i you he she it we they', -.060, .905),
    ('in', -.074, .502),
    ('on at', -.026, .460),
    ('above below', -.498, .984),
    ('around', -.357, .751),
    ('under inside outside behind beneath', -.188, .703),
    ('within between beyond throughout', -.064, .316),
    ('before after during since until', -.168, .493),
    ('for', -.014, .126),
    ('to', -.026, .070),
    ('by', -.057, .083),
    ('with without', -.027, .194),
    ('from', -.030, .302),
    ('near through upon along across against over', .023, .275),
    ('here there herein therein thus itself themselves ahead', -.130, .680),
    ('responsible concerned available involved present relevant', -.140, .696),
    ('prior next adjacent corresponding following preceding surrounding',
     -.085, .587),
)
RESPONSE = {w: (b, g) for words, b, g in RESPONSES for w in words.split()}
RELATIONAL = set('prior next adjacent corresponding following preceding surrounding'.split())
IRREGULAR = set('shown given taken known seen found made left written'.split())
DECAY = (0., 0., 1., .45, .25, .15, .10, .04, .04, .04)

@lru_cache(30000)
def participle(w):
    if w.isascii() and w.isalpha() and 'verb' in wordnet.parts_of_speech(w):
        if w.endswith('ed') or w in IRREGULAR:
            return 2
        if w.endswith('ing'):
            return 1
    return 0

@lru_cache(30000)
def head(w):
    if not w.isascii() or not w.isalpha():
        return False, False, False
    return ('noun' in wordnet.parts_of_speech(w), w.endswith('s'),
            'noun.group' in wordnet.categories(w))


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, '', 99, 99, 99)
    _, tail, dt, da, dd = carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    w = token.strip().lower()
    start = not tail or not tail[-1:].isalpha() or token[:1].isspace()
    value = 0.
    special = w in ('the', 'this', 'these', 'those', 'of', 'que', 'qui', 'che')
    form = participle(w) if start and w not in RESPONSE and not special else 0
    if start and (special or w in RESPONSE or form):
        parts = re.findall(r'[A-Za-z]+|[^\w\s]', tail[-90:].lower())
        prev = parts[-1] if parts else ''
        noun, ends_s, group = head(prev)
        reduced = bool(participle(prev) or prev in RELATIONAL)
        definite = DECAY[dt] if dt < 10 else 0.
        indefinite = 2 <= da <= 6
        demo = dd == 1
        quantified = 0.
        for distance, word in enumerate(reversed(parts[-5:]), 1):
            if not word.isalpha():
                break
            if word in ('all', 'every', 'each', 'both', 'any'):
                quantified = (0., .5, 1., .5, .3, .15)[distance]
                break
        cue = (.078 - 1.213 * definite + .186 * indefinite
               - .325 * demo - .179 * reduced - .141 * ends_s
               - .745 * quantified - .226 * group
               - definite * (.895 * noun + .751 * ends_s + .281 * group))
        if w == 'the':
            value = (-.034 - 1.256 * definite + .127 * indefinite
                     + .065 * reduced + .041 * ends_s - .232 * quantified
                     + definite * (.243 * noun + .321 * ends_s + .071 * group))
        elif w in ('this', 'these', 'those'):
            value = -.029 - .502 * definite - .048 * indefinite
            value += -.161 * definite * noun - .055 * quantified
        elif w == 'of':
            value = .043
        elif w in ('que', 'qui', 'che'):
            value = -.416 - .139 * ends_s
        else:
            base, gain = RESPONSE.get(w, (-.021, .320) if form == 2
                                      else (-.040, .158))
            value = base + gain * cue
    dt, da, dd = min(dt + 1, 99), min(da + 1, 99), min(dd + 1, 99)
    if re.search(r'[.,;:!?]|<\|', token):
        dt = da = dd = 99
    if start:
        if w == 'the':
            dt, da, dd = 1, 99, 99
        elif w in ('a', 'an'):
            dt, da, dd = 99, 1, 99
        elif w in ('this', 'these', 'those'):
            dt, da, dd = 99, 99, 1
        elif w in ('that', 'which', 'who', 'whom', 'where',
                   'is', 'are', 'was', 'were', 'has', 'have', 'had'):
            dt = da = dd = 99
    return (doc, (tail + token)[-120:], dt, da, dd), float(value)

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:5350 -- a "tab indentation / 'if'" detector.

What it does: the component fires on two kinds of token.
  1. Whitespace tokens that contain a tab character (tab indentation, e.g. "\t" or
     "\t       " at the start of a line in code). Its strongest responses are to these.
  2. The word "if" (case-insensitive, with or without a leading space), as in
     "if we set ..." or "... going to ... if he can't", where it begins a conditional.

Everything else is predicted as 0. The values are scaled down (0.45 and 0.3)
because the component is mostly quiet on ordinary text: at full strength the
predictions overshoot and explain negative variance on random positions.

The program only reads the newest token, so it has no carry state.
"""

READS = ()

TAB_WHITESPACE = 0.45  # predicted activation for a tab-containing whitespace token
IF_WORD = 0.3          # predicted activation for an "if" token


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if "\t" in token and token.strip() == "":
        return None, TAB_WHITESPACE
    if token.strip().lower() == "if":
        return None, IF_WORD
    return None, 0.0

"""Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:5351 (a 'bed / bottom' detector).

Its activation is strongly negative on a few words that name a bed or the bottom
of something, and near zero everywhere else. The big case is the token "bed" in
"testbed" (the /testbed repo path in agent transcripts), where it sits near -5.7.
The Chinese word 底 ("bottom") and its compounds (到底, 彻底, 月底, 年底) are about
as strong; the English words " bed", " floor" and the Chinese 床 (bed) are weaker.
"""

# Strong: "bed" glued to "test" (the /testbed path), and the Chinese "bottom" family.
TESTBED_BED = -5.7
BOTTOM_WORDS = {"底": -7.5, "到底": -7.0, "彻底": -6.0, "月底": -5.6, "年底": -4.4, "抵": -5.2}
# Weaker: other bed / floor words.
BED_FLOOR_WORDS = {" bed": -1.5, " Bed": -1.2, "Bed": -1.8, " beds": -2.0, " floor": -1.2,
                   "loor": -3.1, "床": -2.4, "顶": -2.0, "頂": -1.6}

READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2] if len(prefix) > 1 else ""
    if tok == "bed" and prev.endswith("test"):
        return None, TESTBED_BED
    if tok in BOTTOM_WORDS:
        return None, BOTTOM_WORDS[tok]
    if tok in BED_FLOOR_WORDS:
        return None, BED_FLOOR_WORDS[tok]
    return None, 0.0

programs.sol:
"""Approximate a sparse post-predicate signal, mostly negative.

English restrictors and references ("only", "the following", "here", etc.)
receive more negative values after dictionary verbs. Chinese 的 receives a
negative value based on verbal dictionary senses and word frequency, strengthened by
relative-clause, subject-pronoun, and date cues. Japanese endings are recognized by
spelling. Repeated middle-dot punctuation is a separate positive response.
This is a grammatical approximation, not a complete parser.
"""
import math
import opencc
import re
from functools import lru_cache
import cedict
import regex
import wordfreq
import wordnet

READS = ()
SIMPLIFY = opencc.OpenCC("t2s")
AUXILIARIES = frozenset('be am is are was were been being have has had do does did '
                        'can could will would shall should may might must'.split())
PREPOSITIONS = frozenset('of for by in to through with on from at into'.split())
ENGLISH_CUES = frozenset(('only', 'following', 'here', 'both', 'either', 'place'))

@lru_cache(maxsize=10000)
def verb_flags(word):
    """Verb sense, verb without a noun sense, and inflected verb form."""
    if word in AUXILIARIES:
        return 0, 0, 0
    parts = wordnet.parts_of_speech(word)
    bases = wordnet.base_forms(word, 'verb')
    return ('verb' in parts, 'verb' in parts and 'noun' not in parts,
            bool(bases) and word not in bases)


def english_value(word, left):
    words = re.findall('[A-Za-z]+', left.lower())
    prev = words[-1] if words and re.search('[A-Za-z]$', left) else ''
    context = prev
    if prev in {'not', 'the', 'a', 'an'} and len(words) > 1:
        context = words[-2]
    verb, pure, inflected = verb_flags(context)
    auxiliary, preposition = prev in AUXILIARIES, prev in PREPOSITIONS
    if word == 'only':
        return (-.09 - .44*verb - .62*pure - .08*inflected
                - .24*auxiliary - .21*preposition - .27*(prev == 'not'))
    if word == 'following':
        if prev != 'the':
            return -.03
        return -.58 - .49*verb - .45*pure + .15*inflected
    if word == 'here':
        return .01 - .16*verb - .73*pure + .03*inflected
    if word in {'both', 'either'}:
        return .08 - .34*verb - .24*pure - .24*auxiliary - .37*preposition
    if word == 'place' and prev in {'take', 'takes', 'took', 'taking', 'taken'}:
        return -.94
    return 0.0


def chinese_value(token, left):
    left += token.split('的', 1)[0]
    for n in range(min(4, len(left)), 0, -1):
        word = left[-n:]
        glosses = cedict.glosses(word)
        if glosses:
            break
    else:
        return .10
    verbs = [g for g in glosses
             if g.startswith('to ') and not g.startswith('to be ')]
    fraction = len(verbs) / len(glosses)
    frequency = max(0, 9 + math.log10(
        wordfreq.get_frequency_dict('zh').get(SIMPLIFY.convert(word), 1e-9)))
    value = .10 - .30*(glosses[0] in verbs)
    strength = .06 + .26*frequency + .98*(token == '的') - .32*(n > 1)
    value -= fraction * strength
    before = left[:-n]
    if verbs:
        value -= 2.45 * ('所' in before[-4:])
        value -= 2.15 * bool(re.search('[我你他她它您们們]$', before))
        value -= 1.38 * bool(re.search('[年月日]$', before))
    return value


def japanese_value(s, previous):
    if not regex.fullmatch(r'\p{Hiragana}+', s):
        return 0.0
    if s.endswith('のは'):
        return -1.26
    passive = '(られ|され|われ|れ)' + '(る|た|ます|ている|ていた|ています)$'
    if re.search(passive, s):
        return -1.55  # Passive and potential forms.
    if re.search('(て|で)(いる|いた|います|いました)$', s):
        return -1.46  # Progressive forms.
    if s.endswith(('ない', 'ません')):
        return -.77
    if s.endswith(('ます', 'ました')):
        return -.45
    if s.endswith('た'):
        return -.61
    if s.endswith(('る', 'たい')) or s == 'す':
        return -.59
    if s in {'もの', 'こと'}:
        return -.10 - .60*previous.endswith(('た', 'る'))
    return -1.13 if s == 'ような' else 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    old, previous = (b'', '') if carry is None or carry[0] != doc else carry[1:]
    raw = prefix.token_bytes[-1]
    token = raw.decode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    left = old.decode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    s = token.strip()
    value = -.0006
    if s.lower() in ENGLISH_CUES:
        value += english_value(s.lower(), left)
    if '的' in token:
        value += chinese_value(token, left)
    value += japanese_value(s, previous)
    if s and set(s) == {'·'} and (left.endswith('·') or not left):
        value += 1.0
    return (doc, (old + raw)[-100:], token), float(value)

"""Layer-1 MLP neuron 5352 (a single hidden unit of the MLP that down_proj reads).

What it does: the component is this one unit, written into the residual stream. The unit
is strongly negative on words that close a modifier and set up the noun that comes next:

- Chinese 的 right after a verb, i.e. a relative clause ("所引发的种种", "发起的"):
  strongly negative. 的 after a noun, or after a pronoun such as 我 or 自己 (possessive):
  about zero. The verb test is a rough one: the last character of the preceding word is in a
  list of characters that end common Chinese verbs.
- Japanese verb and adjective endings (る, た, い, す): moderately negative; the
  progressive and passive forms (ている, している, された, される): strongly negative.
  Particles and copulas (の, て, を, が, です) are near zero.
- English attributive words: "following" (most after "the"), "only" (most after "not"),
  "herein", "either", "here", "both", "place": mildly to moderately negative.

Everything else predicts 0. Only the previous token within the same document is read.
"""

READS = ()

# Characters that end common Chinese verbs (a rough word class, not a full lexicon).
VERB_END = set(

The unit is silent in English, code and most other text. Inside Italian passages it switches
on, most strongly on Italian words and word pieces (a word's first or middle piece, such as
"sost" in "sostituisce" or "ric" in "ricominciato"), and more weakly on Italian function
words and on word-final pieces.

The program reads the text so far, word by word, and counts Italian and English function
words. Its carry holds, per document (reset at each new document), the counts for the whole
document and for the last 20 counted words. From each count it takes an Italian share,
(Italian + 0.5) / (Italian + English + 1), and cubes the product of the two shares, so only
passages that are clearly Italian switch the unit on. The current token then sets the size:
an alphabetic word piece with a leading space is full size, an alphabetic piece without one
is about half, and punctuation, digits and English words are nearly zero. A final 0.5 is the
scale that best fits the measured activations.
"""

ITALIAN = set("""di che il la è un una per non con del della delle dei degli gli le lo nel nella
nelle nei negli sono si ma come anche più questo questa questi queste alla al alle dal dalla dai
sul sulla sui ed sia ci mi ti ho hanno essere molto tutti loro suo sua suoi sue ad da e o ai ha
era dopo quando perché già cui ogni stato stata fare anni ancora dove può quello quella
nostro nostra tra fra essa esso ne se io tu noi voi lui lei hanno avere fatto""".split())
ENGLISH = set("""the of and to is that it for with as was on be this are by you not or from have
an at which they their there were been has he she we our your will can would""".split())

READS = ()
WINDOW = 20


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: (Italian count, English count, last counted words as 'i'/'e') for this document
    new_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    n_it, n_en, recent = (0, 0, ()) if new_doc or carry is None else carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip().lower()
    if word in ITALIAN or word in ENGLISH:
        recent = (recent + ("i" if word in ITALIAN else "e",))[-WINDOW:]
        n_it += word in ITALIAN
        n_en += word in ENGLISH
    share = (n_it + 0.5) / (n_it + n_en + 1.0)
    local = (recent.count("i") + 0.5) / (len(recent) + 1.0)
    if not word.isalpha() or word in ENGLISH:
        piece = 0.1
    elif token.startswith(" "):
        piece = 1.0
    else:
        piece = 0.5
    value = 0.5 * (share * local) ** 3 * piece
    return (n_it, n_en, recent), value

The token may be a complete function word or the beginning of a longer word.
Pulse strength varies by grammatical class. Sentence-ending punctuation and

only a small response. Document-initial Title: and Java package headers are
separate motifs. Most small background fluctuations are left at zero.

    # other Romance articles
    (0.62,

    # Romance source and interior prepositions
    (0.83,

    # other Romance prepositions
    (0.31,

     "Du Por Per Para Con Com Sur Sous"),
    # Slavic Cyrillic prepositions
    (0.70,
     "В С У К О З На До "
     "За По"),
    (0.12, "W V Z Pod Nad Od Bez"),  # Slavic Latin prepositions
