for strength, words in CLASSES:
    for word in words.split():
        PARTICLES.setdefault(word, strength)

FRAGMENT = 0.08
RESET = 1.22
NEWLINE = 0.03
SPACE = 0.30
SENTENCE = 0.53
CAPITAL = 0.07
OTHER = 0.05
UNSPACED = 0.35

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc, token = prefix.document_ids[-1], prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        previous, position = "", 0
    else:
        _, previous, position = carry
    carry = (doc, token, position + 1)

    if position == 1 and previous == "Title" and token == ":":
        return carry, -11.0
    if position == 0 and token == "package":
        return carry, -0.82
    if position == 1 and previous == "package" and token == " com":

                         and (len(word) == 1 or word[1:].islower()))
        if not short_capital:
            return carry, 0.0
        strength = FRAGMENT

    ending = previous.rstrip()
    if position == 0 or "<|" in previous:
        damping = RESET
    elif "\n" in previous:
        damping = NEWLINE

        damping = SPACE

    return carry, -max(0.0, strength - damping)

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:5354 -- a sentence/phrase-opening function-word detector.

What it does: this component writes a negative value into the residual stream when the
current token is a capitalized function word that typically opens a phrase or sentence:
an article, a preposition or a conjunction such as "The", "In", "On", "At", "By", "To",
"For", "And", "But", or its German, French, Spanish, Italian or Portuguese counterpart
("Das", "Dans", "Eine", "En", "Por", ...). Such words get the value -0.3. Every other token
gets 0.

Why: in the harvested windows, the component's large negative activations (down to about
-2.5) sit almost always on these capitalized opener words, and "In" and "The" are the most
frequent. Lowercase function words ("the", "in") and capitalized content words stay near
zero, and so do pronouns such as "I", "You" and "They". The program reads only the current
token, so its value does not depend on the preceding context.

Limits: the component is large on only a minority of these words, and the program does not
model what decides which ones (it is gated by context the program cannot see). So it captures
only the average effect on these words. Lowercase and mid-word cases, and the rare large
positive values, are not predicted.
"""
READS = ()

ARTICLES = {"The", "A", "An", "Un", "Une", "Eine", "Ein", "Das", "Der", "Die", "El", "Le", "La", "Il"}
PREPOSITIONS = {"In", "On", "At", "By", "For", "To", "From", "With", "En", "Em", "Por", "Dans",
                "Auf", "Mit", "Bei", "Nach"}
CONJUNCTIONS = {"And", "But", "Or", "Doch", "Aber", "Und"}
PRONOUNS = {"We", "Wir", "Es"}
OPENERS = ARTICLES | PREPOSITIONS | CONJUNCTIONS | PRONOUNS
VALUE = -0.3


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[prefix.position].strip()
    if word in OPENERS:
        return None, VALUE
    return None, 0.0

plus ", which" (negative)."""

READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    toks = prefix.token_strings
    cur = toks[-1]
    prev = toks[-2] if len(toks) > 1 else ""
    if prev == " (" and cur == "born":
        return carry, 1.7
    if cur == " which" and prev == ",":
        return carry, -0.8
    if prev in {" is", " was", " are", " were"} and cur in {" a", " an", " the"}:

"""Layer 1 MLP down_proj, component 5357: the "year-opening digit" detector.

What it does: it fires on the second digit of a four-digit year that opens with
"19" or "20", i.e. the "9" in "1978" or the "0" in "2015", in running prose
("born 1975", "in 1950", "since 2001", "June 2018"). Digits inside math or code
(decimals, "radius 2", "2048", "$3.20") stay quiet. Within the year the strength
follows how prose-like the text before it is (the share of letters in the last
60 tokens of text) and is raised when the word just before is a year-introducing
word or a month. Separately, the ".com" token in "github.com" fires strongly.
Everything else is predicted as 0.
"""
READS = ()

MONTHS = {"january", "february", "march", "april", "may", "june", "july", "august",
          "september", "october", "november", "december"}
YEAR_WORDS = {"in", "from", "since", "until", "during", "born", "the", "between", "circa"}
MATH_BEFORE = set(".,=-$+*^")
WINDOW = 60  # tokens of text read before the year
GITHUB_DOMAIN = 2.6
PROSE_SCALE = 2.0
YEAR_BONUS = 0.5
CAP = 2.6


def last_word(text):
    """The last run of letters in text, lowercased ("" if none)."""
    end = len(text)
    while end > 0 and not text[end - 1].isalpha():
        end -= 1
    start = end
    while start > 0 and text[start - 1].isalpha():
        start -= 1
    return text[start:end].lower()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    toks = prefix.token_strings
    n = len(toks)
    cur = toks[-1]
    # The digit that completes "19" or "20" as the opening of a number.
    if n >= 2 and ((cur == "9" and toks[-2] == "1") or (cur == "0" and toks[-2] == "2")):
        before = "".join(toks[max(0, n - 2 - WINDOW):n - 2])
        if before[-1:].isdigit() or before[-1:] in MATH_BEFORE:
            return carry, 0.0  # inside a decimal, a formula or a longer number
        letters = sum(c.isalpha() for c in before) / max(1, len(before))
        word = last_word(before)
        bonus = YEAR_BONUS if (word in YEAR_WORDS or word in MONTHS) else 0.0
        return carry, min(CAP, PROSE_SCALE * letters + bonus)
    if cur == ".com" and n >= 2 and toks[-2] == "github":
        return carry, GITHUB_DOMAIN
    return carry, 0.0

"""Layer 1, MLP down_proj component 5359: a negative detector for the "l" of a "pl"
consonant cluster, when the tokenizer has cut the word around that cluster.

Plain-terms summary. The component goes negative when a word contains the sound "pl":
Latin p+l (plan, plank, planning), Cyrillic п+л (план, пла-), Greek π+λ (πλα-), Polish
p+ł (opłacić). It is strongest on the piece that begins with the "l" right after a "p"
piece ("Pl" + "ank", "п" + "ла", "π" + "λ"), and on the piece right after a piece that
ends in "pl" ("Plan" + "ck", "pl" + "ata"). Weaker: a piece that ends in "pl" (" pl"),
the first piece of a "pla-" word (plan, plane, plate), and later pieces of other pl-words.
Words where "pl" sits inside one token and the word goes on (plural, plain, placing,
plasm, template) stay near zero, as do all words without "pl". Everything else predicts 0.

The program looks back from the current token to the start of its word (a word starts at
a token that begins with a space, newline or punctuation, and never crosses a document
boundary), then checks the word's text for a p-like letter followed by an l-like letter.
"""

READS = ()

P_LETTERS = set("pPпПπΠρΡ")
L_LETTERS = set("lLłŁλΛлЛ")

# predicted activation per situation, from the harvested and sampled data
L_AFTER_P = -1.9        # token begins with l and the token before ends in p: "Pl|ank", "п|ла", "π|λ"
AFTER_PL_PIECE = -1.4   # token continues a word right after a piece that ends in "pl": "Plan|ck"
PL_TOKEN_START = -1.5   # token ends in "pl" and starts a word: " pl", "Pl"
PL_TOKEN = -0.8         # token ends in "pl" inside a longer word
PLA_START = -0.36       # first piece of a word starting "pla-": plan, plane, plate
PL_FIRST_PIECE = -0.13  # first piece of another word containing "pl" inside the piece
PL_CONTINUATION = -0.26 # later piece of a word containing "pl"


def _starts_word(s):
    """A token that begins a new word: whitespace, or punctuation/digits (not a letter)."""
    return s == "" or s[0] in " \n\t\r" or (not s[0].isalnum() and ord(s[0]) < 128)


def _ends_pl(s):
    return len(s) >= 2 and s[-2] in P_LETTERS and s[-1] in L_LETTERS


def _has_pl(text):
    return any(text[q] in L_LETTERS and text[q - 1] in P_LETTERS for q in range(1, len(text)))


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    strings = prefix.token_strings
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    i = prefix.position
    cur = strings[i].lower()

    # the word ending at token i: from its first token (a word-starting token) to i
    start = i
    while start > 0 and docs[start - 1] == docs[i] and not _starts_word(strings[start]):
        start -= 1
    continues = start < i                 # token i continues a word begun earlier
    prev = strings[i - 1].lower() if continues else ""
    word = "".join(strings[k].lower() for k in range(start, i + 1)).strip()

    if continues and cur[:1] in L_LETTERS and prev[-1:] in P_LETTERS:
        value = L_AFTER_P
    elif continues and _ends_pl(prev):
        value = AFTER_PL_PIECE
    elif _ends_pl(cur):
        value = PL_TOKEN_START if word.startswith("pl") else PL_TOKEN
    elif _has_pl(word):
        if continues:
            value = PL_CONTINUATION
        elif word.startswith("pla"):
            value = PLA_START
        else:
            value = PL_FIRST_PIECE
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return carry, float(value)

What it does, in plain terms:
- On the <|endoftext|> token that closes a document it fires strongly (about +1.85).
- On the first token of a document (the token right after <|endoftext|>, or the first
  token of a row that starts mid-document) it is mildly negative (about -0.27 after
  <|endoftext|>, -0.21 at a row start).
- On a few Chinese words (teaching, production, quality, transport, management,
  technology, construction) it fires moderately, the teaching words most strongly.
- Everywhere else it is 0. The many small, diffuse values it takes on ordinary tokens
  (std about 0.05) are not modelled; they carry most of its effect on next-token
  predictions, so this program does little to that part of the effect.

EOT_VALUE = 1.85
AFTER_EOT_VALUE = -0.27  # first token of a document that follows <|endoftext|>
ROW_START_VALUE = -0.21  # first token of a row that begins mid-document

    "教學": 2.0,

    "质量": 1.0,
    "运输": 1.0,

It fires on the word "large" and its relatives: " large", "Large", "larger",
"largest", "largely", "enlarge", and the Chinese 大型 ("large-scale" / "large type").
"largely" is the strongest single token. "large" is weaker in predicate uses
("is large", "very large") than attributive ones ("a large number"); the program
does not model that difference. Elsewhere it is near zero, with a weak negative
response on words that start with "lam", "lens", "lend", "lent", "lease" or
"league" (lamp, lens, lender).

activation for each word family. Positions off the list predict 0.

LARGELY = 8.0           # "largely" is the strongest single token

The component goes strongly negative on the token that completes a word meaning
"protect", in English and in some other languages:
  - " protect" (about -5), " protects", " protecting", " protector", " protective",
    " protected" and " protection" (about -7.5);
  - the stem in other languages: "Prote|ktor|at" (German Protektorat), "Prote|ger"
    (Spanish proteger), "protégé" (about -11);
  - Chinese 保护, 保護, 防护, 维护 (about -4).
Everything else, including "protein", "protocol", "proton", "protest" and the pieces
that come after a complete stem, stays at 0.

How it works: the program tracks the letters of the word being typed (reset at each
document boundary). It fires at the first token where that word contains a protect-stem,
so a word split over several tokens is recognised at the piece that completes the stem.
Predicting this with a short keyword rule explains about half the variance; the
remainder is spread over many rare tokens and is not captured.

import re

READS = ()

STEMS = ("protect", "protek", "proteg", "protég")
CHINESE = ("保护", "保護", "防护", "维护")
WORD_TAIL = re.compile(r"[^\W\d_]*$")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    prev_doc, prev_word = carry if carry is not None else (None, "")
    if doc != prev_doc:

    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]

    if completes_stem:

            value = -11.0

            value = -5.0
        else:
            value = -7.5
    elif any(c in token for c in CHINESE):
        value = -4.0
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return (doc, word), value

also contribute. Chat boundary markers receive small negative offsets.

import re

    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        spaces, tabs, mark, run = 0, 0, '', 0
    else:
        _, spaces, tabs, mark, run = carry

    if '\n' in token:
        body = token.rstrip('\r\n')
        before = body.rsplit('\n', 1)[-1].rstrip('\r')
        local = len(before) if not before.strip(' \t') else 0
        prior = spaces if '\n' not in body and not before.strip(' \t') else 0
        padding = local + prior
        if padding:
            ntabs = before.count('\t') + (tabs if prior else 0)
            if ntabs:
                value += 1.6
                value += 0.32 * math.log1p(padding - ntabs)
            else:

                          else 1.59 if padding <= 8 else 1.8)
            value += 0.6 * math.log1p(prior)
            value -= 0.12 * (token.count('\n') > 1)
        else:
            first = token.split('\n', 1)[0].strip(' \t\r')
            repeated = (first and len(set(first)) == 1
                        and first[0] in SEPARATORS)

                old = run if not first or first[0] == mark else 0
                char = first[0] if first else mark
                indent = spaces + len(token.split('\n', 1)[0]) - len(first)
                value += -0.48 + 0.72 * math.log1p(len(first))
                value += 0.46 * math.log1p(old)
                if first:
                    value += 0.24 * math.log1p(indent)
                    value += 0.24 * (char in '-—')

        value += 0.15 * ('…' in stripped)
        mixed = (('…' in stripped and '.' in stripped)
                 or (mark == '…' and '.' in stripped))

        value += 0.45 * ('\n' not in token and len(stripped) >= 4)

    value -= 0.09 * (token == '<|im_start|>')

    # Save only suffix counts, not the whole text.
    tail = len(token) - len(token.rstrip(' \t'))

        spaces += len(token)
        tabs += token.count('\t')

    if match:

        run = run + length if length == len(token) and char == mark else length
        mark = char

    return (doc, spaces, tabs, mark, run), float(value)

DOT_RUN = re.compile(r"\.{3,}$")

    if "\n" not in token:
        return 0.0
    body = line + token.split("\n")[0]
    stripped = body.rstrip(" \t")

        if "\t" in trailing or len(trailing) >= 3:
            return 1.7
        return 0.5 if len(trailing) == 2 else 0.1

starts a word, i.e. the French demonstrative "ce" / "Ce" ("dans ce cadre",
"ce pays", "Ce nom"), and on the English word "ceiling" / "ceilings" ("raise the
debt ceiling"). It is near zero elsewhere, with a small negative value on a few
German word fragments ("ich" inside a word, e.g. "Ze-ich-nungen").

The program predicts a fixed negative value for those tokens and 0 otherwise.
Word start is judged from the token itself (a leading space) or from the
previous token ending in a non-letter (after punctuation, a newline or a

CE_INSIDE = -0.5     # "ce" continuing a word
CEILING = -3.3       # "ceiling", "ceilings", "ceil"
ICH_INSIDE = -0.5    # "ich" inside a word (German fragment)

    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2] if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 else ""

or a name is written. Whether a token continues the word before it (no leading space) is
what decides it, so the program rebuilds the word from the tokens:

  * acronyms split over tokens, "MS" + "I" (MSI), "CD" + "I", "FS" + "I":   about -4
  * plurals of acronyms, "RB" + "Is" (RBIs), "IC" + "Is":                  about -4.8
  * whole-token acronyms with a consonant before the I, "DPI", "OCI", "PSI": -2.5 (-1 if 2 letters)
  * mixed-case or lowercase fragments, "Sam" + "i", "Mand" + "i", "c" + "si": -1.1 if the
    word has 3 letters or fewer, -0.9 if it has 4 or 5, zero if longer

on Roman numerals ("II", "III") and on the pronoun "I", which get a small -0.2 like other
I/i endings. Values are in the component's own activation units.

import unicodedata

READS = ()

def letters(text):
    """`text` with fullwidth forms folded to ASCII, leading and trailing non-letters removed."""
    text = unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", text)
    start = 0
    while start < len(text) and not text[start].isalpha():
        start += 1
    end = len(text)
    while end > start and not text[end - 1].isalpha():
        end -= 1
    return text[start:end]


def word_before(pieces):
    """Letters of the word the last piece continues, or "" if it starts a word.

    A piece with a leading space starts a new word; one without it continues the word before
    it, so " RB" + "Is" is "RBIs" and "c" + "si" is "csi"."""
    if pieces[-1].startswith(" "):
        return ""
    before = ""
    for piece in reversed(pieces[:-1]):
        before = letters(piece) + before
        if piece.startswith(" ") or letters(piece) != piece:

    return before

            elif len(word) <= 3:

            elif len(word) <= 5:
                value = -0.9
        elif is_caps and word[-2] not in VOWELS_AND_ROMAN:
            value = -2.5 if len(word) >= 3 else -1.0
        else:
            value = -0.2
    return carry, value

    while back < min(WINDOW, len(doc) - 1) and doc[-2 - back] == doc[-1]:
        back += 1
    window = "".join(prefix.token_strings[len(doc) - 1 - back:])

    # The word being written at this token: its trailing letters.
    found = WORD_END.search(window)
    word = found.group(0).lower() if found else ""
    if word not in VALUES:
        return None, 0.0

    slavic = bool(CYRILLIC.search(window) or SLAVIC_DIACRITICS.search(window))
    greek = len(GREEK.findall(window)) >= 6
    if slavic or greek:
        return None, float(VALUES[word])
    return None, 0.0

"""Layer-1 MLP down-projection component 5372: a "digit two places after a 4" detector.

What it does, in plain terms:
  * Strongest: a digit that comes two digits after a '4' inside a number (the
    digit in between is not itself a 4), e.g. the 0 in "1 4 3 0" or the 2 in
    "4 7 2". Predicted activation about +1.1.
  * Weaker: the same pattern with an '8' two digits back (about +0.2), and any digit
    that is the third or later digit of a run (about +0.03).
  * Negative: a period or closing parenthesis right after a bare letter c/C used as a
    list label ("C." / "c)"), about -0.9.
  * Everything else: 0.

Tokens are looked up only within the same document (the model resets at a document
change). Digits are single tokens in this tokenizer, so "two places back" is two tokens back.
"""

READS = ()

DIGITS = set("0123456789")  # a set, so the empty string is not a digit
BIG = 1.07        # digit, previous digit (not a 4), and a 4 two back
EIGHT = 0.20      # same, with an 8 two back
DEEP = 0.025      # third or later digit of a run of digits
ENUM = -0.90      # '.' or ')' right after a list label c / C


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    toks = prefix.token_strings
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    t = len(toks) - 1

    def back(k):
        # token k steps before the current one, or "" across a document boundary
        i = t - k
        if i < 0 or docs[i] != docs[t]:
            return ""
        return toks[i]

    cur, one, two = back(0), back(1), back(2)
    value = 0.0
    if cur in DIGITS and one in DIGITS:
        if two == "4" and one != "4":
            value = BIG
        elif two == "8":
            value = EIGHT
        if two in DIGITS:
            value += DEEP
    if cur in (".", ")") and one in ("c", "C", " c", " C"):
        value = ENUM
    return None, value

"""Recognize value openings in HTML/XML tags and JSX markup.

Quoted attribute values have a modest response (weaker for class and style).
Brace-valued JSX attributes have a much stronger response. A short text tail
provides tag context; document boundaries reset it. Smaller rules recognize
default imports, PHP openings, and JSX className attributes. Child braces
require additional JSX evidence to reduce confusion with JSON and code blocks.
Other text is zero. A conservative overall gain limits overconfident
predictions from syntax alone; this is not a full activation reconstruction.
"""
import re

READS = ()

# Common HTML attributes: these differ consistently in response strength.
QUOTED = {
    'class': 0.55,
    'style': 0.6,
    'href': 1.2,
    'src': 1.8,
    'id': 1.9,
    'for': 1.25,
    'value': 1.7,
    'name': 2.5,
    'target': 2.0,
    'type': 3.2,
    'className': 2.5,
}
MARKUP_ATTRIBUTES = {
    'href', 'src', 'class', 'style', 'className',
    'target', 'rel', 'xmlns', 'border',
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    tail = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else ''
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    value = 0.0
    operator = token.replace('\\', '')
    if token == ' from' and re.search(
        r'\bimport[ \t]+(?:type[ \t]+)?[\w$]+[ \t]*$', tail
    ):
        value = 2.6
    if token == 'php' and tail.endswith('<?'):
        at_start = tail == '<?' or tail.endswith('<|endoftext|><?')
        value = 3.3 if at_start else 1.3
    child = token in ('{', ' {', ' {[', ' {...', '>{')
    if re.match(r'''^=["'“”{]''', operator) or token == ' className' or child:
        context = tail.replace('=>', '')
        opening = context.rfind('<')
        in_tag = opening > context.rfind('>') and bool(
            re.match(r'<[A-Za-z][\w:.-]*(?=\s|/|$)', context[opening:])
        )
        match = re.search(r'([\w:.-]+)\s*$', tail)
        attribute = match[1] if match else ''
        include = re.search(r'{%\s*include\b[^%]*$', context)
        # Event-handler assignments identify a clipped JSX opening tag too.
        event = bool(re.fullmatch(r'on[A-Z]\w*', attribute))
        fragment = bool(re.search(r'\bon[A-Z]\w*=\{[^<>]*$', context))
        jsx = fragment or 'className' in context or '<>' in context
        if token == ' className' and in_tag:
            value = 3.5
        elif operator.startswith('={') and (in_tag or fragment or event):
            value = 9.5 if in_tag or fragment else 7.5
            if operator.startswith(('={(', '={{')):
                value = 7.5
        elif re.match(r'''^=["'“”]''', operator):
            if in_tag or include or attribute in MARKUP_ATTRIBUTES:
                value = QUOTED.get(attribute, 2.8)
                if '\\' in token:
                    value += 1.3
        elif child:
            after_tag = re.search(
                r'<[^<>]*>\s*(?:\d+\s*\t\s*)?$', context
            )
            if token == ' {...' and in_tag:
                value = 5.5
            elif jsx and ((token == '>{' and in_tag) or after_tag):
                value = 5.5 if token == '>{' else 7.5
                if '[' in token:
                    value = 4.5
    return (doc, (tail + token)[-600:]), 0.75 * value

"""Attribute values opened inside a markup tag (HTML, XML, JSX).

Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:5373 responds to the token that opens an
attribute's value inside an open tag. The strongest case is the `={` of a
JSX expression attribute, as in <Category name="All" id={cat.id}>, where
the activation is about 10. The plain `="` (or `=\\"` in an escaped string)
inside a tag, as in <a href="...">, is about 2. Outside a tag, `={` is
about 1 and `="` is about 0.25 (plain code or prose). Everything else is
near zero, so the program predicts 0 there.

The program tracks, token by token, whether it is inside an open tag: a
'<' followed by a letter opens one, and a '>' closes it unless it is the
'>' of an arrow '=>'. The state resets at each document boundary.
"""

READS = ()

IN_TAG_BRACE = 9.7   # `={` inside an open tag: JSX expression attribute
IN_TAG_QUOTE = 2.5   # `="` or `=\"` inside an open tag
OUT_BRACE = 1.2      # `={` outside any tag
OUT_QUOTE = 0.25     # `="` outside any tag


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, False, False, "")
    _, in_tag, after_lt, last = carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]

    value = 0.0
    if in_tag:
        if "={" in token:
            value = IN_TAG_BRACE
        elif "=" in token and '"' in token:
            value = IN_TAG_QUOTE
    else:
        if "={" in token:
            value = OUT_BRACE
        elif '="' in token:
            value = OUT_QUOTE

    # Update the tag state character by character.
    for ch in token:
        if ch == "<":
            after_lt = True
        elif after_lt and (ch.isalpha() or ch == " "):
            if ch.isalpha():
                in_tag, after_lt = True, False
        elif ch == ">" and last != "=":
            in_tag, after_lt = False, False
        else:
            after_lt = False
        last = ch

    return (doc, in_tag, after_lt, last), value

"""Russian '-тель' detector (layers.1.mlp.down_proj:5375).

Fires on the subword piece that completes the letters т-е-л inside a word, in a
-тель ending (учитель, житель, строитель, зритель, пользователь, преподаватель),
and more weakly on the pieces after it in the same word (учителем, зрителя,
свидетельство). Word-initial pieces (телефон, действительно) and тело/тела
(body) stay at 0. Separately, the English word "editor" (text-editor, Editor,
/editor) pushes the activation negative; identifiers with an underscore
(_editor) are left at 0, since they barely move it.
"""

COMPLETE = 5.0     # piece that completes тел
AFTER = 2.0        # later piece of the same word
EDITOR = -3.0      # any piece containing "editor"
ENDINGS = "ьяиюе"  # what may follow тел in -тель, -теля, -тели, -телю, -телей


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    raw = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    tok = raw.lower()
    new_doc = prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    word, prev_alpha = ("", False) if new_doc or carry is None else carry
    # a piece continues the previous word, or the row starts mid-word
    mid = (prev_alpha or new_doc) and tok[:1].isalpha()
    if not mid:
        word = ""
    before = len(word)
    for ch in tok:
        word = word + ch if ch.isalpha() else ""
    value = 0.0
    k = word.find("тел")
    if mid and k >= 1:
        after = word[k + 3:k + 4]
        if after == "" or after in ENDINGS:
            value = COMPLETE if k + 3 > before else AFTER
    if "editor" in tok and "_" not in tok:
        value = EDITOR
    return (word, bool(tok) and tok[-1].isalpha()), value
